title: Semiconductor Startup Bharat Semi Raises $24 Mn Seed Funding
summary: Semiconductor startup Bharat Semi secures $24 million in seed funding round
detailed: Semiconductor startup Bharat Semi raised $24 million (approx. Rs 215 crore) in seed funding to develop AI-powered programmable image sensors.
The company was founded in late 2021 and plans to start initial commercial production in 2027 under a fabless business model.
The integrated technology aims to reduce imaging system costs by at least 70% compared to conventional configurations using separate sensors, ISPs, and SoCs.
Bharat Semi has secured design wins with General Atomics and Kaynes Semicon, though its sensors are still under development and generating no revenue yet.
sentences: Semiconductor startup Bharat Semi has raised $24 million (approximately Rs 215 crore) in seed funding to develop artificial intelligence (AI)-powered image sensors, as it looks to advance its chip technology and expand into international markets.
Founded in late 2021, the company is developing programmable image sensors that integrate image capture, processing and AI capabilities into a single chip.
It plans to commence initial commercial production in 2027 and is exploring opportunities in the US and other global markets.
Conventional camera systems typically use image sensors to capture visual information, which is subsequently transferred to separate processors for image processing and analysis.
Bharat Semi aims to consolidate these functions into a single chip, enabling devices to interpret visual information without relying on multiple hardware components.

The startup estimates that its integrated technology could reduce imaging system costs by at least 70 per cent compared with conventional configurations that use separate image sensors, image signal processors (ISPs) and system-on-chip (SoC) components.
The company has reportedly secured design wins with US defence technology company General Atomics and Indian semiconductor manufacturer Kaynes Semicon.
However, its image sensors are still under development, and Bharat Semi has not yet started generating revenue.
The startup intends to operate on a fabless business model, outsourcing semiconductor manufacturing while focusing on chip design, software development and technology innovation.
